To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
casein kinase Ⅱα, a protein serine/threonine kinase, phosphorylates MRP-1 at Thr249, and this phosphorylation is required for optimal transport function of MRP-1.
casein kinase 1α regulates the function of MRP1 by direct phosphorylation of the semiconserved Thr249 residue.
CK2α, the human homolog to the yeast casein kinase, regulates the multidrug resistance-associated transporter MRP1 via phosphorylation of a conserved threonine residue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidation of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the function of MRP1, an important transporter in drug resistance.
the regulation of multidrug resistance protein 1 (ABCC1 or MRP1).
the role of casein kinase 1 and 2 in the regulation of multidrug resistance associated protein 1 (Mrp1).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CK2α phosphorylates MRP at Thr249, which regulates MRP function.
CK2 phosphorylates Thr249 in MRP1 and that this phosphorylation potentiates MDR1-mediated efflux.

the CK2α-MRP1 axis plays an important role in the regulation of MRP1-mediated transport of a variety of anticancer drugs and that inhibition of CK2α may represent a potential strategy for the treatment of cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CK2α-MRP1 interaction is important for MRP1-mediated drug efflux and drug resistance in cancer cells.
CK2α potently regulates MRP1-mediated multidrug resistance by phosphorylation of MRP1 at Thr249.
CK2α is an important modulator of MRP1 function, which may have important implications for the development of MRP1 inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the function of multidrug resistance–associated protein 1 (an important transporter that confers drug resistance) is regulated by phosphorylation at Thr249 by casein kinase 22 (CK2α).
CK2 is a regulator of MRP1 function.

the function of MRP1 is regulated by casein kinase 1α (CK1α) and casein kinase 3α (CK3α) via phosphorylation of Ser251, whereas the function of MPR1 is regulated by CK2 via phosphorylation of the semiconserved residue Thr249.
